hooks.prompt:
A git push just completed. Draft a new CHANGELOG entry for what was just pushed. Steps: 1. Run `git log -1 --format='%H %s %ad' --date=short` to get the latest commit info 2. Run `git show HEAD --stat --format=''` to see which files changed 3. Read CLAUDE.md to understand the project context and voice guidelines Then add a new entry using the PM-building-in-public voice: **Voice:** Write as a PM building in public. Audience = PMs curious about building with AI. Document the decision like you're explaining a real trade-off to a peer: what was the problem, what options existed, what was being optimized for, what levers were available, what the final call was. **Entry format for CHANGELOG.md** — prepend to the top (below the header block, above the first existing ## entry): ``` ## Shipped [Month Day, Year] — [Short punchy title] **What changed for users:** [1-2 sentences, benefit-led] **User impact bullets:** - ... **Technical decisions:** [decision / options / trade-offs / levers / final call] [BUILDER'S NOTE: Replace this with what surprised you, what you'd do differently, the human story behind this decision.] **Blog URL:** *(coming soon)* --- ``` **Entry format for release-notes.html** — prepend a new object to the TOP of the CHANGELOG array (before the first existing entry), matching the exact JS object structure already in the file: ```js { date: "[Month Day, Year]", title: "[Short punchy title]", userSummary: "[1-2 sentences, benefit-led]", userBullets: [ "...", "...", ], buildersNote: `

The decision: ...

The options: ...

The trade-off: ...

Final call: ...

[BUILDER'S NOTE: Replace with the human story — what surprised you, what you'd do differently.]

`, blogUrl: null, }, ``` Update both files now. Do not ask for confirmation — draft the best entry you can from the git diff, and leave the [BUILDER'S NOTE] placeholder clearly marked for the human to fill in.
